title: What the Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal for partners is, how a partner signs in, and where its settings, admins, audit logs, policy templates and tenants are covered

prose.label: Signing in.

prose.label: Where each area is covered.
prose.text: Partner account settings, white labeling and SSO are in [[shared.multi-tenant-portal.account-settings]]. Admins, roles and scopes are in [[shared.multi-tenant-portal.administration]]. The portal's own audit logs are in [[shared.multi-tenant-portal.audit-logs]]. Policy templates are in [[shared.multi-tenant-portal.policy-templates]]. The tenant list and tenant groups are in [[shared.multi-tenant-portal.tenants]]. The per-tenant details page is in [[shared.multi-tenant-portal.tenant-details]].

purpose.statement: The Multi-Tenant Portal is used by Zscaler partners to manage their provisioned customers and tenants, which can use different Zscaler clouds.

quotes: The Zscaler Multi-Tenant Portal is used by Zscaler partners so that they can manage their provisioned customers and tenants. These provisioned customers and tenants can use different Zscaler clouds based on their access.

hierarchy.statement: A partner can have multiple customers, each customer might have multiple tenant organizations linked under it, and the portal shows this hierarchy from the partner account.

quotes: A Zscaler partner can have multiple customers, and each customer might have multiple tenant organizations linked under them. Through the Multi-Tenant Portal, a partner can view this hierarchy from their partner account.

key-features.statement: The key features listed are oversight of customers across Zscaler clouds, visibility of customer and tenant configurations and policies, white labeling of tenant admin portals, predefined policy templates, and SSO access to tenant admin portals.

quotes: A single interface that allows you to oversee customers across different Zscaler clouds.
In-depth visibility over the customer and tenant account configurations and policies.
Ability to white label the admin portals that your tenants access.
Swift configuration process by predefining policy templates to apply them on to your customers.
SSO (Single Sign-On) access to the admin portals that your tenants access.

first-access.statement: Zscaler Support configures a default admin role with access to all Multi-Tenant Portal functions and emails a request that the password be reset for that role.

quotes: Zscaler Support configures a default admin role, which has access to all the functions in the Multi-Tenant Portal, and sends you an email requesting the password be reset for that role.
After you reset that password, you can access the Multi-Tenant Portal.

login-defaults.statement: The login page language defaults to English (US), and partners who have moved to Authentication Service are redirected to the Authentication Service SSO screen after the Login ID screen.

quotes: For partners who have moved to Authentication Service, the login page redirects to the Authentication Service SSO screen after the Login ID screen.

session-timeout.statement: The Multi-Tenant Portal logs a user out automatically after 15 minutes of inactivity.

quotes: If you are inactive for 15 minutes, the Multi-Tenant Portal automatically logs you out.

upgrade-maintenance.statement: The Multi-Tenant Portal cannot be accessed during an upgrade; a maintenance page is shown for the active upgrade period.

quotes: You cannot access the Multi-Tenant Portal during an upgrade. A maintenance page is displayed during the active upgrade period.

authentication-service-icon.statement: The icon that opens the partner Authentication Service Admin Portal is visible only to users who have migrated to Authentication Service and have the permissions to access and manage the Multi-Tenant Portal within it.

quotes: Click the Authentication Service icon to access the partner Authentication Service Admin Portal.
This icon is only visible to users who have migrated to Authentication Service and possess the necessary permissions to access and manage the Multi-Tenant Portal within Authentication Service.

navigation-items.statement: The Account icon in the left-side navigation shows account information such as the partner account name and admin user ID.

quotes: The Multi-Tenant Portal has the following items in the left-side navigation:
Click the Account icon to see your account information, such as your partner account name and the admin user ID.

session-timeout-auth-service.title: Whether the 15-minute idle logout applies to partners signed in through Authentication Service
session-timeout-auth-service.detail: The access article gives a 15-minute idle logout for the Multi-Tenant Portal and separately redirects migrated partners to the Authentication Service SSO screen; it does not say which session timeout governs the portal after that redirect.
